chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Mu'mmar ibn Khallad and Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Isa, all from Mu'mmar ibn Khallad, from Abu al-Hasan al-Thani (peace be upon him), who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) looked at a man who was saying, 'O Allah, I ask You from Your permissible sustenance.' So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'You ask for the food of the Prophets. Say, O Allah, I ask You for extensive, goodly sustenance from Your sustenance.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended way to ask for sustenance in supplication according to the Imams?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (AS) refines the concept of *rizq* by distinguishing between mere permissibility (*halal*) and the elevated quality of Prophetic sustenance. He advises replacing the generic request for 'permissible sustenance' with the Quranic phrase 'extensive and goodly sustenance,' emphasizing that true spiritual and material abundance requires both breadth and purity. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on elevating supplications to match the spiritual station of the Ahl al-Bayt, moving beyond basic legality to divine excellence.
